questions.q: Two wires of same length and radius are joined end to end and loaded. The Young's moduli of the materials of the two wires are ${Y}_{1}$ and ${Y}_{2}$. The combination behaves as a single wire then its Young's modulus is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In series combination,& $\Deltal = {ℓ}_{1} + {ℓ}_{2}$

$Y = \dfrac{F / A}{\Deltaℓ / ℓ} ⇒ \Deltaℓ = \dfrac{Fℓ}{AY}$

$⇒ \Deltaℓ ∝ \dfrac{ℓ}{Y}$

Equivalent length of rod after joining is $= 2ℓ$

As, lengths are same and force is also same in series

$\Deltaℓ = \Delta{ℓ}_{1} + \Delta{ℓ}_{2}$

$\dfrac{ℓeq}{Yeq} = \dfrac{ℓ}{Y1} + \dfrac{ℓ}{Y2} ⇒ \dfrac{2ℓ}{Y} = \dfrac{ℓ}{Y1} + \dfrac{ℓ}{Y2}$

$∴ Y = \dfrac{2{Y}_{1}{Y}_{2}}{{Y}_{1} + {Y}_{2}}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)
Assertion (A) : The property of body, by virtue of which it tends to regain its original shape when the external force is removed, is Elasticity.
Reason (R) : The restoring force depends upon the bonded inter atomic and inter molecular force of solid.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Elasticity is the ability of a material to deform under stress and then return to its original shape when the stress is removed.

The restoring force in elastic materials is associated with the inter-atomic or inter-molecular forces that act to bring the atoms or molecules back to their original positions when the material is deformed. When an external force is applied to a material, it causes a displacement of atoms or molecules from their equilibrium positions. The restoring force is a result of the potential energy stored in these inter-atomic or inter-molecular bonds, and it works to bring the material back to its original state.

Hence, both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation (A)

questions.q: The bulk modulus of a liquid is $3 \times {10}^{10}{Nm}^{- 2}$. The pressure required to reduce the volume of liquid by $2 %$ is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Bulk modulus& $B = \dfrac{Volumetricstress}{Volumetricstrain} = \dfrac{- ∆ P}{\dfrac{∆ V}{V}}$

Then,~$∆ P = B \times \left(- \dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right) = 3 \times {10}^{10} \times \dfrac{2}{100} = 6 \times {10}^{8}Nm^{- 2}$

questions.solution:
$\dfrac{du}{dv} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ stress $\times \dfrac{stress}{y}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{F^{2}}{A^{2}y}$
$\dfrac{du}{dv}\alpha\dfrac{1}{d4}$
$\dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{du}{dv}\right)}_{1}}{{\left(\dfrac{du}{dv}\right)}_{2}} = \dfrac{{d}_{2}^{4}}{{d}_{1}^{4}} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$\dfrac{{d}_{1}}{{d}_{2}} = {\left(4\right)}^{1 / 4}$
$\dfrac{{d}_{1}}{{d}_{2}} = \sqrt{2}: 1$

questions.q: Young’s moduli of the material of wires A and B are in the ratio of& $1: 4$, while its area of cross sections are in the ratio of $1: 3$. If the same amount of load is applied to both the wires, the amount of elongation produced in the wires A and B will be in the ratio of [Assume length of wires A and B are same]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the elongation of a metallic wire because of the application of a load can be written as

$\Delta$L = \left(\dfrac{FL}{AY}\right)
. . . \left(1\right)$

The ratio of the elongations for both the wires is, then, calculated as follows-

$\begin{cases}\dfrac{∆ {L}_{1}}{∆ {L}_{2}} & = & \dfrac{\dfrac{FL}{{A}_{1}{Y}_{1}}}{\dfrac{FL}{{A}_{2}{Y}_{2}}} \\ & = & \dfrac{{A}_{2}{Y}_{2}}{{A}_{1}{Y}_{1}} \\ & = & \dfrac{3}{1} \times \dfrac{4}{1} \\ & = & \dfrac{12}{1}\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: Under isothermal condition, the pressure of a gas is given by& $P = aV^{– 3},$ where~$a$~is a constant and~$V$& is the volume of the gas. The bulk modulus at constant temperature is equal to
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The data given is&

$P = aV^{- 3}$

Bulk modulus is given by,

$B = - \dfrac{dP}{\dfrac{dV}{V}} = - V\dfrac{dP}{dV}$

$= - V\dfrac{d}{dV} \left\${\dfrac{a}{V3}\right

$= - $V\left[\dfrac{- 3a}{V4}]$

= \dfrac{3a}{V3} =3P

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as& Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion (A) : Steel is used in the construction of buildings and bridges.
Reason (R) : Steel is more elastic and its elastic limit is high.&

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are correct~and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are correct but $R$ is~NOT~the correct explanation of $A$
$A$ is correct but $R$ is not correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relationship between Young's modulus, stress, and strain is:

$\dfrac{stress}{strain} = Y$

Since the elastic modulus of steel is more, for the same amount of stress, the strain will be less resulting in less& deformation of buildings and bridges. Therefore,& steel is used for construction of& large structures.&

Hence, both assertion and reason are correct and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.q: The elastic limit of brass is $379$ MPa. The minimum diameter of a brass rod if it is to support a $400N$ load without exceeding its elastic limit will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Stress $= \dfrac{F}{A}$
Elastic limit is $379$ MPa
$⇒ 379 \times {10}^{6} = \dfrac{400}{A} = \dfrac{400}{\pid^{2} / 4}$
$d = \sqrt{\dfrac{400 \times 4}{\pi \times 379 \times {10}^{6}}}$
$= 1.16 \times {10}^{- 3}m$
$= 1.16mm$

questions.q: Choose the correct relationship between Poisson ratio  \left(\sigma\right)$,~bulk modulus $( K )$ and modulus of rigidity  \left(η\right)$ of a given solid object:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The relations& of Young's modulus,& $Y$, bulk modulus,~$K$, the modulus of rigidity,~$η$~and Poisson's ratio,~$\sigma$~are given as

$Y = 3K ( 1 - 2\sigma ) \ldots \left(1\right)$~and~

$Y = 2η \left(1 + \sigma\right) \ldots \left(2\right)$

From equation~ \left(1\right)and \left(2\right)$, we have

$⇒ 2η \left(1 + \sigma\right) =3K \left($1 - $2\sigma\right)

$⇒ \sigma = \left(\dfrac{3K - 2η}{6K + 2η}\right)$

questions.q: The length of metallic wire is ${l}_{1}$ when tension in it is ${T}_{1}$. It is ${l}_{2}$ when the tension is ${T}_{2}$. The original length of the wire will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming Hooke's law to be valid

$T ∝ \left(\Deltaℓ\right)$

$T = k \left(\Deltaℓ\right)$

Let,${ℓ}_{0} =$ natural length (original length) $⇒ T = k \left(ℓ - {ℓ}_{0}\right)$

so, ${T}_{1} = k \left({ℓ}_{1} - {ℓ}_{0}\right)$& {T}_{2} = $k\left({ℓ}_{2} - {ℓ}_{0}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{T1}{T2} = \dfrac{{ℓ}_{1} - {ℓ}_{0}}{{ℓ}_{2} - {ℓ}_{0}}

$⇒ {ℓ}_{0} = $\dfrac{{T}_{2}{ℓ}_{1} - {T}_{1}{ℓ}_{2}}{{T}_{2} - {T}_{1}}

$

questions.q: A cube of metal is subjected to a hydrostatic pressure $4$ GPa. The percentage change in the length of the side of the cube is close to : (Given bulk modulus of metal,~$B = 8 \times {10}^{10}Pa$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$B = - \dfrac{∆ P}{\dfrac{∆ V}{V}}$
$\dfrac{∆ V}{V} = - \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$
Magnitude is given by,
\left|\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right| = \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$

Volume in terms of length can be represented as,

$3 \times \left|\dfrac{∆ L}{L}\right| = \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$

Therefore,

\left|\dfrac{∆ L}{L}\right| = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$

Substituting the values we get,
\left|\dfrac{∆ L}{L}\right| = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{9}}{8 \times {10}^{10}} = \dfrac{1}{60}$

Percantage change is,
$\dfrac{1}{60} \times 100 = \dfrac{5}{3} = 1 . 67$

$

$ρ = \dfrac{M}{V}$

$- \dfrac{dV}{V} = \dfrac{P}{k}$

$\dfrac{dρ}{ρ} = \dfrac{P}{k} ⇒ dρ = \dfrac{ρP}{k}$

questions.q: A steel wire of length $3 . 2m  \left({Y}_{S} =2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}\right)$ and a copper wire of length $4 . 4m  \left({Y}_{C} =1 . 1 \times {10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}\right)$ , both of radius $1 . 4mm$~are connected end to end. When stretched by a load, the net elongation is found to be $1 . 4mm$. The load applied, in Newton, will be: (Given $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When two wires are connected end to end, the tension in them will be same.

Change in length using Hooke's law can be found as,

$Y = \dfrac{Fl}{A ∆ l} ⇒ \Deltal = \dfrac{Fl}{AY}$

Total change in length can be written as,

$\Deltal = \Delta{l}_{1} + \Delta{l}_{2}$~ ~

$⇒ \Deltal = \dfrac{F{l}_{1}}{{A}_{1}{Y}_{1}} + \dfrac{F{l}_{2}}{{A}_{2}{Y}_{2}}$

$⇒ F = \dfrac{\Deltal}{\dfrac{l1}{{A}_{1}{Y}_{1}} + \dfrac{l2}{{A}_{2}{Y}_{2}}} = \dfrac{1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 3}}{\dfrac{3 . 2}{\pi\left(1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)2 \times 2 . 0 \times {10}^{11}} + \dfrac{4 . 4}{\pi\left(1 . 4 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)2 \times 1 . 1 \times {10}^{11}}} ⇒ F = 1 . 54 \times {10}^{2} = 154N$

Acceleration of the system, $a = \dfrac{3g}{9} = \dfrac{10}{3}ms^{- 2}$

Now, for $R$ we can write

$⇒ {T}_{1} = 20N$

Therefore, strain developed in wire $B$,

$\text{strain} = \dfrac{stress}{Y} = \dfrac{\dfrac{T1}{A}}{Y} = \dfrac{\dfrac{20}{0 . 005 \times {10}^{- 4}}}{2 \times {10}^{11}}$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 4}$

questions.q: A sample of a liquid is kept at 1 atm. It is compressed to 5 atm which leads to change of volume of $0.8 \mathrm{~cm}^3$. If the bulk modulus of the liquid is 2 GPa , the initial volume of the liquid was _______ litre.  \left(\right.$ Take \left.1 \mathrm{~atm}=10^5 \mathrm{~Pa}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, Initial pressure of liquid \left(P_i\right)=1 \mathrm{~atm}$
Final pressure of liquid \left(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{f}}\right)=5 \mathrm{~atm}$
Change in pressure $(\mathrm{dP})=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}=4 \mathrm{~atm}$
$=4 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~Pa}$
Change in volume $(\mathrm{dV})=-0.8 \mathrm{~cm}^3$
Bulk modulus $(B)=2 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~Pa}$
Now, $B=\frac{-d P}{(d V / V)} \Rightarrow V=-B $\left(\frac{d V}{d P})
$\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow & V=-2 \times 10^9 \times \frac{\left(-0.8 \times 10^{-6}\right)}{4 \times 10^5}\\ & =4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^3=4 \text { litre }
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A square aluminium (shear modulus is $25 \times {10}^{9}{Nm}^{- 2}$) slab of side $60$ cm~and thickness $15$ cm is subjected to a shearing force (on its narrow face)$ of 18 . 0 \times {10}^{4}N$. The lower edge is riveted to the floor. The displacement of the upper edge is _____~$\mum$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Shearing stress& is given by& $\dfrac{F}{A} = η\dfrac{x}{l}$

Thus, displacement is~$x = \dfrac{Fl}{Aη}$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{18 \times {10}^{4} \times 60 \times {10}^{- 2}}{60 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 15 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 25 \times {10}^{9}}$

$= 48 \times {10}^{- 6}m = 48\mum$

questions.q: The area of cross-section of a railway track is $0 . 01m^{2} .$ The temperature variation is $10 ° C .$ Coefficient of linear expansion of material of track is ${10}^{- 5} C - 1 ∘ .$ The energy stored per meter in the track is $Jm^{- 1} .$ (Young's modulus of material of track is ${10}^{11}Nm^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Elastic energy $= \dfrac{Y}{2} ( strain{)}^{2} \times$ Area $\times$ length

$⇒$ Elastic energy per unit length $= \dfrac{Y}{2} ( strain{)}^{2} \times$ Area

$($strain $= \dfrac{\Deltaℓ}{ℓ} = \alpha\DeltaT = {10}^{- 5} \times 10 = {10}^{- 4} )$
$= \dfrac{{10}^{11}}{2} \times {\left({10}^{- 4}\right)}^{2} \times {10}^{- 2} = 5Jm^{- 1}$

questions.q: The elastic behaviour of material for linear stress and linear strain, is shown in the figure. The energy density for a linear strain of $5 \times {10}^{- 4}$ is _____ $kJm^{- 3}$. Assume that material is elastic upto the linear strain of $5 \times {10}^{- 4}$,
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the above graph, we can find that when the strain is $5 \times {10}^{- 4}$ the stress is $100$ MPa. We know that energy density is

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times stress \times strain$$⇒ U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 100 \times {10}^{6} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 4}$

$⇒ U = 2 . 5 \times {10}^{4}Jm^{- 3} = 25kJm^{- 3}$
